1.q: בֶּן־שְׁתֵּ֨ים עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה בְ⁠מָלְכ֔⁠וֹ וַ⁠חֲמִשִּׁ֤ים וְ⁠חָמֵשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּ⁠ירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְ⁠שֵׁ֥ם אִמּ֖⁠וֹ חֶפְצִי־בָֽהּ
1.note: In this verse and the next verse, the author is introducing **Manasseh** as a participant in the story as the new king of Judah. Since there were no more kings of Israel, from this point on the author no longer refers to a year in the reign of the king of Israel to identify when a king began to reign Judah. So to translate this verse, see how you translated the similar expressions in 8:26 and similar verses.

2.note: To translate the expression **in the eyes of Yahweh** here and in verse 6, see how you translated the similar expression in 3:2. Alternate translation: [And he did what Yahweh considered to be evil]
See how you translated the similar expression in 16:3. Alternate translation: [on account of]
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:12. Alternate translation: [the Israelites]

3.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 1:11. Alternate translation: [And he once more built] or [And he rebuilt]

To translate the expression **the whole army of the heavens** here and in verse 5, see how you translated the similar expression in 17:16. Alternate translation: [to all the lights in the sky] or [to the heavenly bodies here]

4.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 5:18. Alternate translation: [in the temple of Yahweh]

Here, the **name** of Yahweh represents people calling on him by name as their God and thus worshiping him. If it would be helpful in your language, here and in verse 7, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. If you have already translated the book of 1 Kings, see how you translated the similar expression in 1 Kings 8:16. Alternate translation: [I will make Jerusalem a special place for people to worship me]

5.note: By **the two courts**, the author is referring to the inner court, where the priests offered sacrifices, and the outer court, where other Judeans could go. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [in the inner and outer courtyards of the temple of Yahweh]

6.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 16:3. Alternate translation: [And he burned his son completely as an offering to an idol]

A **ritual pit** was a hole in the ground that was used in ceremonies to try to contact the spirits of dead people. If your readers would not be familiar with what a ritual pit was, in your translation you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a general expression. If you have already translated the book of 1 Samuel, see how you translated the same expression in 1 Samuel 28:3. Alternate translation: [a place to use to try to contact dead people]

The expression **familiar spirits** describes supernatural beings that people in this culture believed existed and could help them gain secret knowledge. If your readers would not be familiar with this, in your translation you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a general expression. If you have already translated the book of 1 Samuel, see how you translated the same expression in 1 Samuel 28:3. Alternate translation: [for spirits that people believed could give them secret knowledge]

The author is using **multiplied doing evil** as a common expression of his culture to mean “did very many evil things.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [He did evil after evil] or [He did very many evil things]

7.q: בַּ⁠בַּ֨יִת הַ⁠זֶּ֜ה וּ⁠בִ⁠ירוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר בָּחַ֨רְתִּי֙ מִ⁠כֹּל֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אָשִׂ֥ים אֶת־שְׁמִ֖⁠י לְ⁠עוֹלָֽם
7.note: If you have already translated the book of 1 Kings, see how you translated the similar expression “for my name to be there” in 1 Kings 8:16. In the context of the expression here **I will put my name**, the term **name** could refer to: (1) Yahweh providing a place for people to call on him by name as their God and thus worship him. Alternate translation: [I will make this temple in Jerusalem, which I have chosen from all of the tribes of Israel, a special place for people to worship me] or (2) Yahweh providing a place that would promote his reputation. Alternate translation: [I will make this temple in Jerusalem, which I have chosen from all of the tribes of Israel, a place that will promote my reputation]

Here the **tribes of Israel** represent their territories. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from the whole territory of Israel]

8.note: Yahweh, envisioning all the Israelites as if they were a single person, their ancestor **Israel**, is using one part of that person, his **foot**, to mean all of him in the act of wandering. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I will not add to make the Israelites wander]

Yahweh is using **I will not add to make** as a common expression of this culture to mean “I will not again make.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I will not make the Israelites wander again]
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:24. Alternate translation: [to their ancestors]

9.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 21:2. Alternate translation: [on account of the Israelites]

10.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 9:36. Alternate translation: [through the agency of his servants the prophets]

11.note: The author is not referring to a specific **Amorite**. He means the Amorites in general. (The verb translated as **did** is plural.) If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the Amorites did who were to his face]
See how you translated the similar expression in 17:2. Alternate translation: [who was before him]

12.q: לָ⁠כֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הִנְ⁠נִי֙ מֵבִ֣יא רָעָ֔ה עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וִֽ⁠יהוּדָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֙ כָּל־שמעי⁠ו תִּצַּ֖לְנָה שְׁתֵּ֥י אָזְנָֽי⁠ו
12.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [therefore Yahweh, the God of Israel, says to behold him, bringing disaster on Jerusalem and Judah that everyone hearing it, the two of his ears will tingle]

Yahweh is using a physical sensation that people will have (their **ears** will **tingle**) to represent the emotion that people will feel when they hear about this disaster. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. If you have already translated the book of 1 Samuel, see how you translated the similar expression in 1 Samuel 3:11. Alternate translation: [that will horrify everyone who hears about it]
See how you translated the similar expression in 19:7. Alternate translation: [I am about to bring]

13.q: וְ⁠נָטִ֣יתִי עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אֵ֚ת קָ֣ו שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן וְ⁠אֶת־מִשְׁקֹ֖לֶת בֵּ֣ית אַחְאָ֑ב
13.note: A **measuring line** is a cord with markings on it that is used to determine length. A **plumb line** is a weight on the end of a cord that is used to determine whether a wall is straight upright. Alternate translation: [And I will measure Jerusalem with the same marked cord that I used to measure Samaria, and I will determine whether Jerusalem is upright by using the same weight on the end of a cord that I used to determine whether the house of Ahab was upright]

13.q: וְ⁠נָטִ֣יתִי עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אֵ֚ת קָ֣ו שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן וְ⁠אֶת־מִשְׁקֹ֖לֶת בֵּ֣ית אַחְאָ֑ב
13.note: If builders using a **measuring line** or **plumb line** discovered that a structure was not the right size or that a wall was leaning, they would tear down the structure or wall. Yahweh is using these instruments to represent the standards by which he judged and punished the people of **Samaria** (the northern kingdom of Israel) and the descendants of **Ahab**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. The UST models one way to do that.

13.q: וּ⁠מָחִ֨יתִי אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם כַּֽ⁠אֲשֶׁר־יִמְחֶ֤ה אֶת־הַ⁠צַּלַּ֨חַת֙ מָחָ֔ה וְ⁠הָפַ֖ךְ עַל־פָּנֶֽי⁠הָ
13.note: The point of this comparison is that just as a person who ensures that he has wiped a **dish** thoroughly by turning it over and wiping both sides, so Yahweh will **wipe Jerusalem away** thoroughly and completely. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [And I will wipe Jerusalem away just as thoroughly as a person wipes a dish who turns it over to make sure that he has wiped both sides]

Yahweh is using the term **face** to mean the “front” of this **dish**. If this term does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and turns it over and also wipes the back]

14.q: וְ⁠נָטַשְׁתִּ֗י אֵ֚ת שְׁאֵרִ֣ית נַחֲלָתִ֔⁠י וּ⁠נְתַתִּ֖י⁠ם בְּ⁠יַ֣ד אֹֽיְבֵי⁠הֶ֑ם וְ⁠הָי֥וּ לְ⁠בַ֛ז וְ⁠לִ⁠מְשִׁסָּ֖ה לְ⁠כָל־אֹיְבֵי⁠הֶֽם׃ יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשׂ֤וּ אֶת־הָ⁠רַע֙ בְּ⁠עֵינַ֔⁠י וַ⁠יִּהְי֥וּ מַכְעִסִ֖ים אֹתִ֑⁠י מִן־הַ⁠יּ֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָצְא֤וּ אֲבוֹתָ⁠ם֙ מִ⁠מִּצְרַ֔יִם וְ⁠עַ֖ד הַ⁠יּ֥וֹם הַ⁠זֶּֽה
14.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could create a verse bridge and put verse 15 before verse 14, since verse 15 gives the reason for the result that verse 14 describes. Alternate translation: [And because they have done evil in my eyes and they have been making me angry from the day that their fathers came out from Egypt and to this day, I will abandon the remnant of my inheritance, and I will give them into the hand of their enemies. And they will become spoil and plunder for all of their enemies]

14.q: וְ⁠נָטַשְׁתִּ֗י אֵ֚ת שְׁאֵרִ֣ית נַחֲלָתִ֔⁠י וּ⁠נְתַתִּ֖י⁠ם בְּ⁠יַ֣ד אֹֽיְבֵי⁠הֶ֑ם וְ⁠הָי֥וּ לְ⁠בַ֛ז וְ⁠לִ⁠מְשִׁסָּ֖ה לְ⁠כָל־אֹיְבֵי⁠הֶֽם
14.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh says that he will abandon the remnant of his inheritance, and he will give them into the hand of their enemies. And they will become spoil and plunder for all of their enemies]

Yahweh is speaking of the people of Israel as if they were something that he had inherited as a lasting possession. He is referring to the Israelites as the people who were supposed to belong to him perpetually. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. If you have already translated the book of 1 Samuel, see how you translated the similar expression in 1 Samuel 10:1. Alternate translation: [my people, who were supposed to belong to me perpetually]
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:10. Alternate translation: [and I will allow their enemies to have power over them]

The terms **spoil** and **plunder** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [And all of their enemies will plunder them completely]

15.q: יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשׂ֤וּ אֶת־הָ⁠רַע֙ בְּ⁠עֵינַ֔⁠י וַ⁠יִּהְי֥וּ מַכְעִסִ֖ים אֹתִ֑⁠י מִן־הַ⁠יּ֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָצְא֤וּ אֲבוֹתָ⁠ם֙ מִ⁠מִּצְרַ֔יִם וְ⁠עַ֖ד הַ⁠יּ֥וֹם הַ⁠זֶּֽה
15.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh says that he will do this because they have done evil in his eyes and they have been making him angry from the day that their fathers came out from Egypt and to this day]

16.q: וְ⁠גַם֩ דָּ֨ם נָקִ֜י שָׁפַ֤ךְ מְנַשֶּׁה֙ הַרְבֵּ֣ה מְאֹ֔ד
16.note: The author is using the expression **poured out … blood** to represent killing, since blood pours out of people when they are killed violently. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And Manasseh also killed very many innocent people] or [And Manasseh also had very many innocent people killed]

The author is using the term **mouth** to mean “end” or “side.” If this term does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar expression in 10:21. Alternate translation: [until he filled Jerusalem from one end to the other] or [until he filled Jerusalem completely]

The author is speaking as if Jerusalem had been a container and Manasseh had actually **filled** it with blood. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [until people had been killed violently in every part of Jerusalem]

17.q: וְ⁠יֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֤י מְנַשֶּׁה֙ וְ⁠כָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וְ⁠חַטָּאת֖⁠וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטָ֑א הֲ⁠לֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַ⁠יָּמִ֖ים לְ⁠מַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה
17.note: In this verse and the next verse, the author is concluding the story of Manasseh. To translate this verse, see how you translated the similar phrases in 1:18.

The author is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [and the sins that he committed]

18.note: See how you translated the same expression in 8:24. Alternate translation: [And Manasseh passed away] or [And Manasseh died]

The expression **was buried** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and people buried him]

19.q: בֶּן־עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וּ⁠שְׁתַּ֤יִם שָׁנָה֙ אָמ֣וֹן בְּ⁠מָלְכ֔⁠וֹ וּ⁠שְׁתַּ֣יִם שָׁנִ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ בִּ⁠ירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְ⁠שֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔⁠וֹ מְשֻׁלֶּ֥מֶת בַּת־חָר֖וּץ מִן־יָטְבָֽה
19.note: In this verse and the next three verses, the author is introducing **Amon** as a participant in the story as the new king of **Judah**. To translate this verse, see how you translated the similar expressions in 8:26.

21.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 8:18. Alternate translation: [And he lived just as his father had lived]

22.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 8:18. Alternate translation: [and he did not live as Yahweh wants people to live]

24.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 3:23. Alternate translation: [But the people of the land killed]

Since the author has already used the expression **the people of the land** earlier in this sentence, it may be more natural in your language to use a pronoun here. Alternate translation: [and they made Josiah his son reign]

25.q: וְ⁠יֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י אָמ֖וֹן אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲ⁠לֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַ⁠יָּמִ֖ים לְ⁠מַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה
25.note: In this verse and the next verse, the author is concluding the story of Amon. To translate this verse, see how you translated the similar phrases in 1:18.

26.note: Here the author is using the pronoun **one** in a general sense, not to refer to a specific person. Use an expression for this that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And he was buried]
